newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may see 17.3 mln bag coffee crop - Caceer.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may see 17.3 mln bag coffee crop - Caceer.

text.p: Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop could fall to 17.3 million 60-kg bags against 24.5 million bags harvested in 1996/97, said the head of the Co-operatives Center in the Cerrado area of Minas Gerais state (Caceer).
The center reached its estimate by speaking to technicians in 12 key areas in Brazil, either in person or on the telephone, said Edmundo Aguinaldo.
The sharp fall Aguinaldo attributed to many areas experiencing an "off" year in Brazil's two-year production cycle in which there is a larger harvest every other crop.

This has been accentuated by trees still showing the effects of two frosts and a drought in 1994 which effectively halved the 1995/96 harvest and from which the Brazilian tree population is still recovering.
"Many trees became so dehydrated....agronomists are still looking for the answers to what they are seeing at the moment," Aguinaldo said.
- south of Minas 4.4 million to 4.7 million
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
